Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen, China (Hu, Wang, Gao); Independent Researcher, China (Peng); Singapore Management University (Lo)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — CLI-Tool-Bench, a structure-agnostic benchmark for 0-to-1 generation of CLI tools from an empty workspace, with automated black-box differential testing against human-written oracle repositories; 7 LLMs x 2 agent frameworks compared

No SDD approach. 14 configurations: agent frameworks OpenHands (with CodeAct) and Mini-SWE-Agent (versions not stated) x models GPT-5.4, Claude-Sonnet-4.6, DeepSeek-V3.2, Qwen-3.5-plus, GLM-5, MiniMax-M2.5, Kimi-k2.5

Task prompt only (no scaffold): sanitised functional context from the README, full iteratively extracted '--help' documentation ('strict external interface specification'), and one verified execution example per command pattern; anonymised (no author names or GitHub links)

Agent: single trajectory from prompt and empty workspace; explores, writes and executes code with unlimited turns, no iteration or token limit, no external test feedback; ends on the agent's own termination signal. Benchmark pipeline: repository curation -> schema-guided task synthesis (schema extraction, LLM-directed fuzzing) -> black-box differential evaluation
None during generation; humans only in curation (stratified manual validation by two SE experts) and in validating the semantic-match judge
Not an SDD workflow; agent frameworks run end to end on the benchmark

New project: generate a complete, installable CLI tool from scratch (0-to-1) in an empty workspace

94 tasks (from 15,000 raw GitHub repositories); oracle size Easy <=1,500 LOC (40, avg 635.90), Medium 1,500-4,000 (21, avg 2,687.57), Hard >=4,000 (33, avg 18,509.97); 50 test cases per command pattern; 14 configurations x 94 repositories, one generation run each

CLI tools in Python (34), JavaScript/Node.js (15) and Go (45); nine domains (web development 8, testing 7, utility libraries 20, machine learning 12, data analysis and processing 11, database interaction 6, networking tools 7, batch file processing 13, system tools 10)

Build (global installation success rate; failure scores zero on all later metrics); Exec (execution reliability, exit code 0 where the oracle succeeds); SP (side-effect pass, file-system changes equal to oracle); behavioural equivalence of stdout: EM (exact match), FM (normalised Levenshtein similarity > tau = 0.8), SM (semantic match judged by GPT-5.4); macro-averaged over command patterns
Repository structure: total files generated vs human oracle (modularity vs monolithic design); qualitative note on missing defensive programming

Performance by language and by oracle LOC (LOESS trend); phase-based failure shares (build 23.3%, execution 13.2%, behavioural mismatch 6.7% of trajectories); workspace sprawl (local dependency directories); zero-file cases

Automatic: generated and oracle repositories run in two identical Docker containers with snapshot-and-restore; exit code, file-system diff and stdout compared; token and cost logs. SM by GPT-5.4 at temperature 0, validated on 1,000 output pairs by two annotators (>=4 years SE experience), Cohen's kappa > 0.9. Test cases from LLM-directed fuzzing validated against the oracle. McNemar's test and bootstrap (10,000) 95% CIs

Tasks: 94 CLI repositories, same prompts and empty workspace. Configurations: 7 models x 2 frameworks. Baseline: none among configurations; human oracle repository is the reference for behaviour and structure. Held constant: prompt, Docker sandbox without network, no iteration/token limits, no external feedback, evaluation pipeline (auxiliary LLM GPT-5.4, temperature 0). Acceptance tests: black-box differential tests (50 per command pattern) against the oracle. Repetitions: one generation run per configuration; McNemar's test and bootstrap 95% CIs on test-level pass/fail. Human intervention: none

Kimi-k2.5 best (average SM 43.78%; 51.16% with Mini-SWE-Agent), then MiniMax-M2.5 (34.59%); GPT-5.4, Qwen-3.5-plus, GLM-5 about 29-31%; Claude-Sonnet-4.6 lowest (10.61%), mainly failing Build (ends trajectories without compiling). Ranking of the top-tier models reported significant (p < 0.05, McNemar). Mini-SWE-Agent generally above OpenHands (framework average SM 32.50% vs 26.78%). Funnel: Build 76.75% -> Exec 59.32% -> SP 45.66% -> EM 23.50% (FM 39.00%, SM 29.64%). Go weakest language. U-shaped trend with LOC: SM 32.66% (Easy) -> 25.08% (Medium) -> 28.87% (Hard). Tokens do not track performance: GPT-5.4 on Mini-SWE-Agent 31.82% SM with <21K tokens ($0.09); MiniMax-M2.5 on OpenHands 4.21M tokens, 88.02 steps, 30.11% SM. Agents produce monolithic repositories (median 1-3 files) vs modular human oracles

Distinguished models, frameworks, languages and complexity levels; graded metrics (FM, SM) separated functionally correct outputs that EM penalises; SM judge validated (kappa > 0.9). Repeatability: single generation run per configuration, significance from test-level resampling only. Limitations stated: 94 tasks; strict exit-code criterion may count custom non-zero codes as failures; single-trajectory, no-feedback setting only

Dataset scale (94 tasks) traded for quality; strict exit-code alignment; no feedback-driven, multi-turn generation. Gaps: end-to-end behavioural validation needed beyond string metrics; agents need file-system awareness and self-reflection to avoid thrashing; developers should give structural scaffolding, add defensive programming, enforce self-testing. Future: larger dataset, feedback-driven paradigms, other domains (web services, API backends, GUI)

Inconsistencies: text gives Claude-Sonnet-4.6 'averaging 7.58 and 7.09 steps' (Mini-SWE-Agent, OpenHands), but Table III steps are 7.17 and 7.48 (7.58 and 7.09 are its completion-token averages); text says Mini-SWE-Agent 'consistently achieves higher scores', but DeepSeek-V3.2 is lower on Build (72.34 vs 80.85) and equal on SM (27.41 vs 27.44); abstract's 'maximum overall success rate of only 43.8%' is the two-framework average for Kimi-k2.5, whose Mini-SWE-Agent SM is 51.16%; MiniMax '4.21 million tokens' matches prompt tokens only. Values from Tables II and III (pp. 6, 8). Data: scripts, datasets and raw data at github.com/kinesiatricssxilm14/CLI-Tool-Bench. Pre-registration: not stated.
